requirements.description: The supplier identifies a security contact.
The supplier has a documented incident response plan.
The supplier reviews user access at least annually.
The supplier requires multi-factor authentication for all administrator accounts.
The supplier tests restoring backups at least annually.
The supplier has a documented information security policy.
The supplier applies role-based or equivalent structured access controls to staff accounts.
The supplier has documented and implemented safeguards for remote employee workstations.
The supplier has implemented procedures for managing software dependencies and repositories.
The service supports single sign-on for users and administrators.
The service makes audit logs available covering login, logout, actions, timestamps and source IP addresses.
The service automatically locks or ends inactive sessions.
The supplier maintains a systems configuration management strategy.
The supplier scans systems and applications for vulnerabilities and remediates findings before releases.
The supplier has implemented procedures to mitigate security risks while patches are pending.
The supplier separates customer data using documented technical access controls.
The supplier encrypts sensitive data in transit using secure protocols.
The supplier encrypts sensitive data at rest.
The supplier segments trusted and untrusted networks.
The supplier assesses the security of third parties that host or receive customer data.

answers.security_contact: For security matters, contact our security lead Jae at jae@fictional-f.example.
answers.incident_response: Our approved, written playbook explains how staff detect, contain, and respond to security incidents.
answers.access_review: Every three months, managers check and recertify access privileges for every user.
answers.admin_mfa: Every administrator must enter a password and a one-time code from an authenticator app when signing in.
answers.backup_restore: Each quarter we restore a backup into an isolated environment and verify that the recovered application works.

assessments.evidence_quote: For security matters, contact our security lead Jae at jae@fictional-f.example.
assessments.reason: The answer explicitly identifies a named security contact with email details.

assessments.evidence_quote: Every three months, managers check and recertify access privileges for every user.
assessments.reason: Quarterly reviews (every three months) are more frequent than the required annual review, thus satisfying the minimum requirement.

assessments.evidence_quote: Every administrator must enter a password and a one-time code from an authenticator app when signing in.
assessments.reason: The requirement for a password and a one-time code constitutes multi-factor authentication for all administrators.

assessments.evidence_quote: Each quarter we restore a backup into an isolated environment and verify that the recovered application works.
assessments.reason: Quarterly restore tests are more frequent than the required annual testing, thus satisfying the minimum requirement.

answers.access_review: We recertify access for administrators every year. We never review access for other users.

answers.backup_restore: We restore a backup as a test once every eighteen months.

assessments.reason: The supplier explicitly reviews access for administrators annually, but explicitly states that access for other users is never reviewed, meaning only part of the user base is covered.

assessments.evidence_quote: We restore a backup as a test once every eighteen months.
assessments.reason: The supplier tests restores, but the frequency is every eighteen months, which is less frequent than the required annual (every 12 months) testing.

answers.security_contact: Security questions go to our information security lead at security@northbridge.example.
answers.incident_response: We maintain an approved incident response plan and review it annually.
answers.admin_mfa: MFA is enforced for employees with administrator accounts, but contractor administrators are exempt.
answers.backup_restore: We run daily backups. We have not tested restoring a backup.
answers.security_policy: Our information security policy is approved by management and published internally.
answers.staff_rbac: Staff permissions are assigned through role-based access groups.
answers.remote_work: Our documented remote-work standard requires managed devices, encryption and endpoint protection.
answers.software_supply_chain: Dependencies are inventoried and scanned; code changes require repository review.
answers.sso: SAML single sign-on is available for users and administrators.
answers.audit_logs: Customer logs include login and logout timestamps. Actions and source IP addresses are not included.
answers.session_timeout: Inactive sessions are terminated after 20 minutes.
answers.configuration: Configuration baselines are documented, versioned and checked during deployment.
answers.vulnerability_scanning: We scan releases but sometimes deploy before high-risk findings are remediated.
answers.patch_mitigation: We have no documented process for mitigating vulnerabilities while patches are pending.
answers.tenant_isolation: Tenant identifiers and authorization checks separate each customer’s data. The architecture is documented.
answers.transit_encryption: Sensitive data in transit uses TLS 1.2 or later.
answers.rest_encryption: Customer databases and backup storage are encrypted at rest.
answers.network_segmentation: Production workloads run in private segments with restricted connections to public services.
answers.third_party_assessment: Third parties hosting customer data are reviewed before use and reassessed annually.
